newsitem.title: UK: Markka takes ERM place, shares consolidate.
newsitem.headline: Markka takes ERM place, shares consolidate.

text.p: The Finnish markka entered the European Union's currency grid without fuss on Monday, while major European stock markets consolidated recent gains at the start of a new week.
EU finance ministers applauded the markka's smooth entry into the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM), which limits the fluctuations of most current EU currencies against each other.
But they were cautious about the return to the grid of the next candidate in line, the Italian lira.
Wall Street extended Friday's revival with the Dow Jones industrial average of U.S. blue-chip shares, usually a key influence on European markets, breaking back above 6,000.
But traders said early share trading in New York was thin. U.S. bond markets were shut for the Columbus Day holiday and no major U.S. statistics were due for release.
"The strength is a function of the lack of volume more or less," one U.S. share analyst said. "The absence of the bond market and the stable dollar are contributing to the strength."

In the latest step on the road to a single EU currency, Finland agreed at the weekend to put the markka into the ERM. One of the criteria for joining European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) in 1999 is at least two years of ERM membership.
The markka traded around 2.9880 to the German mark in mid-afternoon trading, little changed from Friday's Helsinki close and stronger than its ERM central rate of 3.04.
But its widely signalled entry into the mechanism unsettled forestry stocks in Helsinki, although financial analysts said its rate should not put pressure on exporters.

Traders said the focus was now on the lira and the Swedish crown, which along with the British and Greek currencies were the only EU currencies outside the ERM. Both the lira and crown were firmer at midsession.
After a finance ministers' meeting in Luxembourg, French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said the EU should not be be too hasty in bringing the lira back into the ERM.
"To be hasty on the re-entry (of the lira) would mean to take a risk...which would cause harm to the Italian and European monetary authorities," Arthuis said.

With European currency news taking the spotlight, the dollar largely held its ground and currency dealers said it could receive support from fallout from the Finnish move. The pound hit 2.4192 marks in early trade, its highest level since January 1995, but slipped back later.

European bourses, like Wall Street, had been in buoyant mood on Friday, rising on figures which suggested that inflation in the United States, the world's biggest economy, was being kept in check. But they paused for breath on Monday.

Higher futures and strength in the pound helped the London stock market, Europe's biggest, reverse early losses and edge higher in subdued business as analysts concluded the latest British data showed little sign of inflationary pressure.
Dealers said sentiment was also boosted by a Merrill Lynch fund managers survey which said institutional investors were growing more optimistic about the British stock market.
But political jitters ahead of an election due by May are still a key background concern. "There's still the worry that this government cannot last the full term," one trader said.
French stocks were lower in quiet trading, amid nervousness ahead of a public sector strike on Thursday, but the Frankfurt bourse made moderate gains.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5292 marks and 111.62 yen, compared with 1.5307 and 111.67 in late business on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1430 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was up 4.3 points at 4,032.4 after earlier losing around 11 points.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt ended floor trade on the bourse up 7.85 at 2,693.88. In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was down 7.23 at 2,139.89.
The Dow average in New York was up 32.05 to 6,001.43.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $380.90 an ounce in the afternoon, compared with $381.05 in the morning and a previous London close of $381.35. Silver edged up to $5.04 from $5.02.
